title: Correct a timing-belt end clamp on a handling axis
justification: Festo manufacturer-documented linear handling/assembly axis repair; a plate short of its stop loses pretension in operation. This is a maintenance contribution, not a quantified AI deployment bottleneck.
fault: New belt installed with one end plate short of clamp stop; full final setup pending native contact proof.
instruction: Correct the belt end clamp and finish restoring the linear axis.
objects: New polychloroprene/Glascord toothed belt and original plates, pins and adjusting screws
Source-sized hex drivers; no gripping tabs or added fixture
skill: Physically align four teeth and belt end with the plate, seat against the body stop, retain under manufacturer preload and restore full axis travel.
scoring: Not implemented: observable plate/belt seating and complete repair with actual load/frequency and free travel; all unsupported runtime gates remain required.
risks: No full native belt proven; previous chain family exposed contact/constraint instability
Dominant four-tooth profile and stop must be real collision geometry
Final novelty depends on weakest valid route; tension-only family overlaps2203
Thread engagement and actual gripper reaction loads required
No certification or exact real force calibration claimed
strict_review: Do not submit an isolated clamp coupon or manufacturer label on generic tensioning. No prototype counts as task validation.
